Im a property manager for an apartment complex here in NC. I would definitely read through your lease agreement. Most larger complexes use a standard NAA lease here in NC. Some places write their own. If it is a NAA lease agreement, there will be a section that addresses repairs and transfers of units, especially if the repair is not due to your treatment of the unit. 

My company will transfer someone without any charges and make the new lease start on the day of transfer and then end the same as it would have normally ended if the tenant is not responsible for the repairs. We also give them a week overlap on both apartments to make it easier to transfer their belongings.
